brief.direction: Replacing the glass in a Victorian greenhouse

naturalSourceText: Maintaining a Victorian greenhouse can be a rewarding yet challenging task, especially when it comes to replacing the glass. Over time, the glass panels can become cracked or broken, compromising the structure's integrity and the plants' well-being. To start, gather the necessary tools: safety gloves, a hammer, a putty knife, and replacement glass cut to size. Begin by carefully removing the damaged glass, taking care not to harm the surrounding panels. Use the putty knife to scrape away old putty, ensuring a clean surface for the new glass. Once the old glass is removed, place the new panel into position, securing it with fresh putty. This not only holds the glass in place but also provides insulation. Finally, smooth the putty for a neat finish, and allow it to cure properly. Regular maintenance, including checking for leaks and replacing any damaged glass promptly, will keep your Victorian greenhouse in excellent condition for years to come.
